audit.evidence: Live gate on real Docker: real npm object-path pkg bytes via aliases (0.11.4/0.11.5/0.11.6) driving published withInheritedProps.set() via HTTP. original string __proto__ pollutes+flag@v0, blocked@v1; bypass array [__proto__] key (type confusion) pollutes+flag@v1; residual@v2 blocked (polluted=false, secret denied). passed=true, 4-way closure.

app_purpose: Small JavaScript deep get/set/delete utility library (npm `object-path`, by mariocasciaro); `objectPath.set(obj, path, value)` splits/walks a dotted-string or array key path, creating intermediate objects/arrays, and assigns the leaf value (nested set-by-path). The `withInheritedProps` instance (options.includeInheritedProps) also reads/writes inherited properties along the walk.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in object-path's set() key-walk. The walk dereferences each segment (getShallowProperty then recurses into obj[currentPath]), so a crafted `__proto__` segment makes the walk step OUT of the fresh target and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write ADDS/modifies a property on it. Exploitation requires the `withInheritedProps` instance (options.includeInheritedProps=true): only it walks inherited props AND the __proto__ guard is gated on that flag. The pollution is GLOBAL (mutates real shared Object.prototype), so the harness restores (deletes) the injected property after each probe. The incomplete fix is a string-only `currentPath === '__proto__'` guard bypassed by a NON-string (array) key of the dangerous name = CWE-843 type confusion (CVE-2021-23434).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL VERIFICATION (against the real npm tarballs object-path@0.11.4/0.11.5/0.11.6, index.js set()): 0.11.4 has NO __proto__ guard in set(). The CVE-2020-15256 fix (0.11.5, commit 8e77521) ADDED `if (options.includeInheritedProps && (currentPath === '__proto__' || (currentPath === 'constructor' && typeof currentValue === 'function'))) throw` — a strict `===` STRING comparison of the RAW currentPath with NO type coercion. The CVE-2021-23434 fix (0.11.6, commit 43af2d8) inserted `if (typeof currentPath !== 'string' && typeof currentPath !== 'number') currentPath = String(currentPath)` BEFORE that guard. So V1 (0.11.5) is the guard WITHOUT coercion = the incomplete fix / TARGET; the residual `[['__proto__'],'pcbUnlock']` (a segment that is itself an array) has `['__proto__'] !== '__proto__'` so it slips the V1 guard, yet `obj[currentPath]` stringifies the array back to '__proto__' and still pollutes; V2 (0.11.6) String()-coerces first and catches it. V0 (0.11.4) has no guard so the plain-string seed genuinely pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real same-sink differential). Confirmed empirically on real Docker (see repro.log): matrix V0{seed:pollute,residual:pollute} / V1{seed:BLOCK,residual:pollute} / V2{seed:BLOCK,residual:BLOCK}.

sink: object-path index.js — the set() key-walk magic-property guard on path segments (`var currentPath = path[0]`). The walk dereferences each segment and recurses into obj[currentPath]; a `__proto__` segment, as a STRING (seed) or as a NON-string array element (residual), makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype. Driven via objectPath.withInheritedProps.set() (CVE requires includeInheritedProps).
residual: The string-comparison guard (V1 = object-path@0.11.5) compares the RAW currentPath with strict `===` against the STRING '__proto__' (no coercion). A path whose first segment is itself an array — `[['__proto__'],'pcbUnlock']` — makes the dangerous key the array `['__proto__']`; `['__proto__'] === '__proto__'` is FALSE so the guard passes it, then `obj[currentPath]` coerces the array to the string '__proto__' and the walk steps onto Object.prototype = CVE-2021-23434. The string `['__proto__','pcbUnlock']` seed is blocked on V1; the array-key residual is not.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: GHSA-v39p-96qg-c8rf / CVE-2021-23434: A type confusion vulnerability can lead to a bypass of CVE-2020-15256 when the path components used in the path parameter are arrays. In particular, the condition `currentPath === '__proto__'` returns false if currentPath is `['__proto__']` (an array). This is because the === operator returns false when the operand types are different. Fixed in 0.11.6 by coercing path components to strings before the check.

CVE requires the withInheritedProps instance. Gate passed on real Docker 2026-07-14.
